privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what personal data PlayRPG processes — on our server, in your browser and at third parties — why, for how long, and what rights you have.

sections.title: Data controller
paragraphs: The controller of your personal data is {{name}}, a private individual who runs PlayRPG (playrpg.net) as a private project. For anything concerning your data, write to {{email}}.
Capitalised terms such as Service, Account, Game, Game Master and Content have the meaning given to them in the Terms of Service.

sections.title: Data stored on the server
paragraphs: Account: your e-mail address; your password — only as a hash created with the bcrypt algorithm, from which the password cannot be read; the dates the Account was created and activated; the date and version of the Terms you accepted; one-time tokens for activating the Account and resetting the password (the reset token expires after one hour); whether the Account has administrator rights.
Profile and settings: your avatar, your signature (the name shown to other participants) and interface settings such as the scene control scheme.
Files: images, files and music uploaded to your library, with their names, size, type, folders and playlists.

Games: the Games you create or join and your participation in them (role, date joined, avatar and signature in that Game), Game invitations, and the content of Games — scenes, maps, tokens, fog of war, drawings, notes, handouts, character sheets, chat messages and dice rolls with their author and time.
System templates: templates created in the system creator and the list of people you share them with, with their e-mail addresses and roles.

Statistics and permissions: the results of your dice rolls and the time you spend in Games (start, end and length of the connection), from which we compute the statistics shown in Settings, and the game systems in which you may create Games.

Participants of a Game see your e-mail address (in the player list, and as your name until you set a signature), your avatar and signature, and the Content you share in the Game, as far as the visibility settings allow. People you share a system template with may see your e-mail address.
We do not ask for your name or any data other than described above. Do not put personal data of third parties in Content without a legal basis (see the Terms, section on User Content).

sections.title: Data in your browser
paragraphs: We store in your browser's local storage your login token, your interface language, your music volume, your analytics choice, the language filter on the game list, and which tutorials and which version of the changelog you have already seen. These are required for the Service to work and do not need your consent. We do not share them with third parties.
Cookies are set only by Google Analytics, and only after you consent (see Analytics).

sections.title: Server logs
paragraphs: For every request, the web server logs your IP address, the time, the address of the page opened (without parameters), the response code and size, and your browser information (user agent). These logs serve the security of the Service, detecting abuse and fixing failures. We keep them for up to 14 days.
Application logs contain technical information about requests and errors, without IP addresses. They are deleted once they exceed a size limit and on every update of the Service.

sections.title: Correspondence and e-mails
paragraphs: When you write to us by e-mail or through the contact form, we process your e-mail address, your name if you give it, and the content of your message. A message from the form reaches us by e-mail at {{email}}.

We send you only the e-mails needed to use your Account: the activation link and the password reset link, and where necessary the messages described in the Terms (e.g. about a change to the Terms or a decision concerning Content). We do not send newsletters or advertising.

sections.title: Analytics (Google Analytics 4)
paragraphs: If you accept, we load Google Analytics 4. It stores the cookies _ga and _ga_<ID> on your device and sends Google your IP address, browser information, the pages you open and the actions listed below. Google acts as a separate controller and processes this data outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States.
We measure page views, account registration, e-mail confirmation, logging in and creating a game. We never send your e-mail address or any other data that identifies you directly.
While you are logged in we send Google your account identifier — a random string of characters, never your e-mail. It lets us tell whether the same person came back on another device.

You can withdraw your consent at any time at the bottom of this page, or in Settings, under Privacy, if you are logged in. We then stop sending data and delete the analytics cookies. Declining costs you nothing — the Service works exactly the same.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
paragraphs: Providing the service under the Terms — creating and running your Account, storing and sharing Content, running Games, statistics, activation and password reset e-mails, complaints: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract).

Security and continuity of the Service — server logs, backups, detecting abuse — as well as answering messages and establishing, exercising or defending legal claims: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (our legitimate interest).
Analytics: Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR (your consent).
Handling notices of illegal Content and appeals under the Digital Services Act (DSA) and complying with other legal obligations: Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR.
Providing an e-mail address and a password is voluntary but necessary to create an Account. We do not make decisions about you based solely on automated processing.

sections.title: Recipients of data
paragraphs: OVH — the provider of the VPS in the European Union on which the Service runs and the data described above is stored, and of the mail server through which we send and receive e-mails. OVH processes data on our behalf.
Google — only if you consent to analytics, as a separate controller (see Analytics).
Other Users — as described in the section Data stored on the server. Public authorities — only where the law requires it.
We do not sell data. Apart from Google Analytics, we do not transfer data outside the European Economic Area.

sections.title: Retention
paragraphs: We keep Account data and Content until the Account is deleted. Deleting the Account means deleting the data linked to it, except for backup copies.

Content you delete (e.g. a file, a note, a character) is deleted immediately. A Game deleted by its Game Master is no longer accessible but stays in the database until it is permanently deleted, at the latest when the Game Master's Account is deleted.
Accounts whose e-mail address has not been confirmed are not deleted automatically at the moment. You may request their deletion at any time.

We make backups of the database and files on every update of the Service and remove them in rotation: we keep the last 7 database backups and the last 5 file backups. Data deleted from the Service disappears from backups once the last backup containing it is rotated out.

We keep web server logs with IP addresses for up to 14 days. We keep correspondence for as long as needed to handle it, and then until any related claims become time-barred. Google keeps analytics data for the period set in Google Analytics.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access your data and receive a copy of it, to have it rectified, erased, restricted and ported, and the right to object to processing based on our legitimate interest. You may withdraw your consent at any time; this does not affect the lawfulness of processing before the withdrawal.

To exercise these rights, write to {{email}}, preferably from the e-mail address linked to your Account. We reply without undue delay and within one month at the latest. If a request comes from another address, we may ask you to confirm that the Account is yours.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority — the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych, ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw, Poland, uodo.gov.pl).

sections.title: General provisions
paragraphs: These Terms of Service set out the rules for using PlayRPG, available at playrpg.net (the "Service"), a tool for running tabletop role-playing sessions online.
The Service is provided by {{name}}, e-mail: {{email}} (the "Provider"). We correspond in Polish and English.

Definitions: User — a person using the Service; Account — the data of a User registered in the Service; Game — a virtual session in the Service; Game Master — the User who created a Game; Player — a User taking part in a Game; Content — any material shared by Users, in particular images, files, music, notes, messages, character sheets and game system templates.
Using the Service requires a device with internet access, an up-to-date web browser with JavaScript and WebSocket enabled, and an active e-mail address.
These Terms are available free of charge at playrpg.net/terms in a form that allows them to be saved and printed. The processing of personal data is described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: Account
paragraphs: An Account may be created by a person who is at least 16 years old. By creating an Account, the User declares that they meet this requirement.

Registration requires an e-mail address and a password, acceptance of these Terms and confirmation of the e-mail address via the activation link. Once the Account is activated, an agreement for the provision of electronic services is concluded for an indefinite period.
The User is responsible for keeping their password secret and for actions taken using their Account.

The User may request deletion of their Account at any time by writing to {{email}} from the e-mail address linked to the Account. Deleting the Account terminates the agreement and deletes the Content linked to it, except for backup copies, which are removed as backups rotate.

sections.title: Free service
paragraphs: Using the Service is free of charge.

The Service is a project developed by a private individual and provided as is. The Provider makes efforts to keep the Service running without interruption but does not guarantee its continuous availability or the permanence of stored Content. Users should keep copies of important material outside the Service.
The Provider may temporarily suspend the Service, in particular for maintenance, updates or to fix failures.
Provisions limiting the Provider's liability do not apply to damage caused intentionally or to other cases in which limiting liability is not permitted by law.

sections.title: User Content
paragraphs: Content belongs to the User who shared it or to its rightful owners. The Provider acquires no rights to it.

By sharing Content, the User grants the Provider a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to store, reproduce and display it solely to the extent necessary to provide the service, in particular to the Game participants with whom the User shares it, and in backup copies. The licence expires when the Content or the Account is deleted; backup copies are removed as backups rotate.
The User declares that they hold the rights to the Content they share or use it lawfully, and that sharing it does not infringe the rights of third parties.

The User who shared Content is solely responsible for it. If a third party brings a claim against the Provider concerning a User's Content, the User undertakes, to the extent permitted by law, to indemnify the Provider and cover the costs the Provider incurs.

It is forbidden to share Content that: infringes copyright or other rights of third parties (including scans and excerpts of rulebooks without the rights holder's consent); is unlawful; depicts the sexual abuse of minors; incites hatred or violence against real persons or groups; contains malware; or contains personal data of third parties without a legal basis. Fictional content typical of role-playing games, such as violence or horror, is allowed.
The Provider does not review Content before it is shared.

Anyone, including a person without an Account, may report Content they consider unlawful or contrary to these Terms by writing to {{email}}. A report should include: identification of the Content (e.g. the Game name and a description or screenshot), an explanation, the reporter's name and e-mail address (not required for reports concerning the sexual abuse of children), and a statement that the report is made in good faith and the information in it is true.

The Provider handles reports without undue delay. Where there are reasonable doubts about the legality of Content, the Provider may block access to it while it is being assessed. The reporter is informed of the decision.

If the Provider removes Content, blocks access to it or restricts an Account, the User receives, at the Account's e-mail address, a statement of reasons indicating what the decision concerns, its grounds and how to appeal. An appeal may be sent to {{email}} within 6 months; the Provider handles it within 14 days. Once the infringement is removed, access to the Content may be restored.

sections.title: Intellectual property
paragraphs: The Service, in particular its code, design and branding, is protected by law and belongs to the Provider. Using the Service grants the User no rights to these elements beyond the right to use the Service in accordance with these Terms.
Copying the Service or any part of it and automated collection of data from the Service (e.g. scraping) without the Provider's consent are forbidden.
Names and trademarks of third-party role-playing games belong to their owners. The Service is not affiliated with or endorsed by any game publisher.
Material made available under open licences (e.g. the SRD) is used under the terms of those licences, described on the Licenses page.

sections.title: Rules of use
paragraphs: Users use the Service in accordance with the law, these Terms and good practice.

In particular, it is forbidden to harass other Users, send spam, impersonate others, attempt to gain unauthorised access to Accounts or Games, circumvent the Service's security, or overload the Service.

sections.title: Complaints
paragraphs: Complaints about how the Service works may be sent to {{email}}.
A complaint should include the Account's e-mail address and a description of the problem.
The Provider responds to a complaint within 14 days of receiving it, to the e-mail address it was sent from.

sections.title: Blocking and termination
paragraphs: The User may terminate the agreement at any time by requesting deletion of their Account.

The Provider may block or delete an Account in the event of a serious or repeated breach of these Terms or the law. The User receives a statement of reasons and may appeal under the rules described in the section on User Content.
The Provider may terminate the agreement for other important reasons, in particular if the Service is discontinued, with 30 days' notice sent to the Account's e-mail address.

sections.title: Changes to the Terms
paragraphs: The Provider may change these Terms for important reasons, in particular changes in the law or changes to the Service's features.

Users are informed of a change by e-mail or by a notice in the Service at least 14 days before it takes effect. A User who does not accept the changes may terminate the agreement before that date by requesting deletion of their Account.

sections.title: Final provisions
paragraphs: The agreement is governed by Polish law. This choice of law does not deprive a consumer of the protection afforded by the mandatory provisions of the law of the country of their habitual residence.
Disputes are resolved by the common courts having jurisdiction under general rules.
These Terms are available in Polish and English. In the event of any discrepancy, the Polish version prevails.

help.loadError: This help page could not be loaded. Check your connection and refresh the page.

tutorial.tabsIntro: The right panel holds everything that is not the map. Pick a tab:
tutorial.tabsOutro: Most tabs have their own short tutorial too — look for the question mark next to their heading.

tabs.chat: dice rolls, results and messages from the whole table
tabs.scenes: your maps: switch between them, add new ones, decide who sees which
tabs.handouts: images and documents the GM shares with the table
tabs.music: background tracks played to everyone at once
tabs.notes: your notes — private by default, but you can share one with the table
tabs.players: who joined, who is online, inviting by link, and removing someone from the game
tabs.minigames: dice minigames you can start for the table
tabs.general: game settings, language, control scheme, 3D dice, returning to the game list, or logging out

characterCard.title: Selected character
characterCard.body: A short sheet of the character you clicked: key stats and quick rolls. Click the scroll icon next to the name to open the full sheet in its own window — minimising it parks it in the bar at the top of the screen, so nothing gets lost behind the map.

characterList.title: Character list
characterList.body: Every player character and NPC in this game. Click the arrow button to add one to the first free slot on the map, or click the tile itself to load it into the card above.

sceneSelector.title: Scenes
sceneSelector.body: Your maps. Switch between them, add a new one, and decide which scene each player is looking at — you can preview a scene before you show it to anyone.

windowBar.title: Open windows
windowBar.body: Character sheets, handouts, and notes open as separate windows. Minimising one parks it here, so nothing gets lost behind the map.

body.modern: Scroll to zoom, drag with the right mouse button to pan the map. Left-click a token to select it, drag it to move it — dragging across empty map selects several at once. You can change this in the General tab.
body.classic: Scroll to pan the map, Ctrl+scroll to zoom — dragging with the right mouse button pans as well. Left-click a token to select it, drag it to move it — dragging across empty map selects several at once. You can change this in the General tab.

layerSelector.title: Active layer
layerSelector.body: The map is stacked from layers: tokens, the GM layer, and the background. Pick the layer first — moving or deleting an image or token only affects the layer armed here; drawing is not limited to it.

body.gm: Select and move, measure distance, paint fog of war and draw. Fog is what your players cannot see yet — you uncover it as they explore.
body.player: Select and move your tokens, measure distance to a target and draw on the map so the rest of the table sees what you mean.

combatButton.title: Turn order
combatButton.body: Start combat on this scene. It stays hidden until you show it to the players; add tokens with a right click or from the Combat window.

panelHeader.title: Help and shortcuts
panelHeader.body: The question mark opens a menu: the user guide and what is new in PlayRPG (both in a new tab, so the game stays open), the keyboard shortcuts (or press ?) and a replay of this tutorial. A dot on it means unseen news. Contact, the terms and the privacy policy are linked in the General tab.

onlineUsers.title: Who is here
onlineUsers.body: Everyone in the game. A lit avatar means the person is connected right now. The outline is the player's colour, the same one you see on their ruler, pings and log entries. Click your own to change your avatar, signature, avatar size and colour.

tabsNav.title: Right panel tabs
tabsNav.body: Everything that is not the map lives here — pick a tab to switch the panel.

diceControls.title: Dice and roll visibility
diceControls.body: Roll dice without opening any sheet. The eye picks who sees the result — everyone, the GM only, or you alone — and the filter next to it hides other people's rolls from the log.

body.0: Every roll and message from the table lands here, newest at the bottom. It also looks empty when a filter is hiding everything, not just when nothing has happened yet.
body.1: Every roll and message from the table, newest at the bottom. Hidden rolls show only to the people allowed to see them.

body.gm: The dice icon here rolls a custom combination without opening any sheet. The dropdown at the end of that row decides who sees the result — everyone, you and whoever rolled, you alone, or one participant of your choosing.
body.player: The dice icon here rolls a custom combination without opening your sheet. The dropdown at the end of that row decides who sees the result — everyone, just you and the GM, the GM alone, or one other participant of your choosing.

myRolls.title: Only my rolls
myRolls.body: Hides everyone else's entries from the log, so you can find your own result in a busy fight.

body.0: Your own notes appear here, along with any public notes other players have shared. Yours are private by default, but you can mark one public to share it with the table.
body.1: Your notes, plus any public ones from others. Drag to reorder, click one to edit it — yours stay private by default until you mark them public from inside the editor.

add.title: New note
add.body: Adds an empty note at the top of the list. Useful mid-session for a name you want to remember.

filter.title: Search
filter.body: Filters the list as you type. While a filter is active, dragging to reorder is switched off.

body.0: Maps, tokens and portraits you upload will appear here. Drag a file onto the scene to place it.
body.1: Maps, tokens and portraits. Drag one onto the scene to place it, or hover over it to reveal buttons for cropping, renaming, and deleting it. A fourth button, for adding it to the scene, appears once a scene is open.

createFolder.title: Organising files
createFolder.body: Create folders to keep a long campaign tidy. Drag files between them.

breadcrumb.title: Where you are
breadcrumb.body: The path of the folder you opened. Click an earlier part of it to jump back up — the last part is just your current folder, so clicking it does nothing.

body.0: The maps of this campaign will appear here. Create one to give the table something to stand on.
body.1: The maps of this campaign. Click one to work on it — your players keep seeing whichever scene you assigned them.

create.title: New scene
create.body: Opens a form for the scene's name and grid size. You add a background image and assign players afterward, from the scene canvas and the settings panel below.

settings.title: Scene settings
settings.body: The scene's name, its grid width and height, whether the grid is shown, fog of war, linked music, and which players can see it.

0.gm: Letters, portraits and maps you hand to the players will appear here. Nothing is shared until you say so.
0.player: Anything the GM hands to the table appears here — letters, portraits, maps. Empty for now.

1.gm: Letters, portraits and maps for the players. Each one is shared only with the people you pick.
1.player: What the GM has shared with you. Click one to open it in its own window.

create.title: New handout or folder
create.body: The "+ Add Handout" button uploads a file — an image, PDF or text file — as a handout and lets you choose who can see it. The "+ New Folder" button creates a folder to organise your handouts.

library.title: Your tracks
library.body: Everything you uploaded. Press play on a track to send it to the whole table at once.

nowPlaying.title: Playback
nowPlaying.body: What is playing now, with skip, pause and stop. Everyone hears the same thing at the same moment.

playlists.title: Playlists
playlists.body: Group tracks into a set — tavern, battle, travel — and start the whole set with one click.

volume.title: Two volumes
volume.body: This slider controls the table's overall volume — moving it changes what every player hears. Each player also has their own slider, but that one only adjusts the sound on their end.

inviteLink.title: Invite link
inviteLink.body: The quickest way in: create a link, copy it and paste it on Discord or wherever your group talks. Whoever opens it joins as a player — if they're not logged in, they log in or register first and land in the game afterwards. "New link" replaces it (the old one stops working), "Remove link" turns it off.

invite.title: Inviting players
invite.body: Type in their account email to add them straight to the game — nothing is sent, and they join immediately with no confirmation needed on their end.

body.0: Everyone who joined will appear here, with their email address.
body.1: Every player in the game, not the GM, with their email address. A green dot on their avatar means they are connected right now.

kick.title: Removing a player
kick.body: Takes the person out of this game. Their character stays, so you can share it with somebody else.

list.title: Dice minigames
list.body: Small games for the table — handy while the party argues about which door to open.

start.title: Starting a game
start.body: Pick a game and choose which online players join — offline ones can't be picked. The board pops up for the whole table right away — the people you picked take turns, everyone else just watches. Only one minigame runs at a time.

name.title: Template name
name.body: This is how the system appears in the list when someone creates a game. Every change saves automatically.

tabs.title: Two steps
tabs.body: General holds the settings of the whole system; Sheet is where you build the character sheet itself, field by field.

visibility.title: Who can use and edit it
visibility.body: Owners manage access here. Viewers can use and clone the template, Editors can also change it, Owners can also manage access and delete it. A public template can be used by anyone, but only members can edit it.

about.title: Description and language
about.body: Tell players what this system is about. The description shows next to the template when someone creates a game, and the language lets them find it with the language filter.

sheetWidth.title: Sheet window width
sheetWidth.body: How wide the character sheet opens for players. The Sheet tab shows the sheet at exactly this width.

dice.title: Dice under the chat
dice.body: Choose which quick-roll dice buttons appear under the chat in games using this system.

modifier.title: Roll modifier
modifier.body: When on, every roll from this sheet first asks the player for a modifier: either a number, such as a bonus or a penalty from the situation, or edge and setback dice that roll again and keep the best or the worst result.

successLevels.title: Success levels
successLevels.body: Choose how the log grades a roll: a signed number of levels per step, or named thresholds such as half or a fifth of the target, each in its own colour.

token.title: Token display
token.body: Decide what a character's token shows on the map, e.g. a health bar or states read from fields on the sheet.

help.title: Help is always here
help.body: Click the question mark to replay the tutorial of the tab you are on.

palette.title: Components
palette.body: Click a field type to add it to the active section — its name is shown above the list. Click any element on the sheet to make its section active. Types are grouped: layout, character, stats, text, choice and tables.

body.0: The sheet is empty. Start with a section — the box that holds fields and decides how many columns they sit in.
body.1: This is the sheet exactly as players will see it: the same width and the same look. Hover an element and click the pencil in its toolbar to edit it.

section.title: Sections
section.body: A section groups fields under a heading and splits them into columns. Sections can be nested; drag one by its handle to move it.

field.title: Fields
field.body: Hover a field to see its toolbar: drag handle, move up and down, edit, duplicate and delete. The pencil opens the field's properties: label, values, rolls and display options. The question mark in that window's title bar explains the field you are editing.

preview.title: Clean preview
preview.body: Hide every editing tool to see the sheet exactly as a player will.

status.title: Saving
status.body: How many sections and fields the sheet has. Every change saves automatically — there is no save button.

help.title: Help is always here
help.body: Click the question mark to replay this tutorial. A field's properties window has its own question mark that explains that field.

body.section: A section holds fields under a heading and arranges them in columns.
body.char_name: The character's name, shown on the character list and next to the map token. One per sheet.
body.char_avatar: The character's portrait, used on the character list and as the map token. One per sheet.
body.image: An image the player uploads to the sheet, e.g. a coat of arms or a sketch.
body.attr: An attribute: a number the player can roll against, optionally split into a base value and advances.
body.attr_table: A table of attributes sharing one set of settings — handy for a whole set such as strength, agility and intelligence.
body.number: A plain number the player types in, e.g. money or experience. Formulas can read it.
body.computed: A value calculated from a formula over attributes and numbers. The player cannot type into it.
body.progress: A current/maximum pair shown as a bar, e.g. health or mana.
body.text_short: A single line of text, e.g. profession or origin.
body.text_long: A multi-line text area, e.g. a backstory or notes. It can also get a formatting toolbar.
body.checkbox: A yes/no tick, e.g. a condition or an ability already used.
body.select: A choice from a list you define, e.g. race or class.
body.skill_table: A list of skills with values the player rolls against. Players can add their own if you allow it.
body.weapons_table: A table of weapons with your columns, an attack roll and a damage formula.
body.data_table: A table with your own columns for anything that is not rolled, e.g. equipment.
body.skill_tree: Skills arranged in a hierarchy, e.g. a skill and its specialisations.
body.label: Fixed text on the sheet — a heading, a hint or a rule reminder. It holds no value.

body.default: How the field looks on the sheet.
body.skill_table: The favourites star, a development mark for skills used this session, alphabetical order and a two-column layout.
body.skill_tree: The favourites star, a development mark for skills used this session, alphabetical order and a two-column layout split by branch.
body.weapons_table: Sort the rows by a short-text column you pick, and split the table into two columns.
body.data_table: Sort the rows by a short-text column you pick, and split the table into two columns.
body.text_long: Turn on text formatting: headings, colours, lists and links, with the same toolbar as notes. The field grows to four rows to fit it.

body.default: The label players see, an optional abbreviation for compact views, and whether the field also appears on the short character card.
body.label: The text shown on the sheet, its colour and its size. The internal name only identifies the label here in the creator.

body.default: The field's starting value, limits and step.
body.attr: Minimum, maximum, starting value and step. Turn on advances to split the value into a base plus advances.
body.number: Minimum, maximum, starting value and the step of the arrow keys.
body.skill_table: Turn on advances to give every skill a base value plus advances; the base can come from the linked attribute.

body.default: The attributes in this table: name, abbreviation, starting value and limits. Drag a row by its handle to reorder it.
Build the value from blocks: attributes, numbers, constants and operators. The sheet recalculates it as values change.

body.select: The options the player chooses from.
body.skill_table: The skills on the list with an optional starting value, optionally linked to an attribute, and whether players may add their own. Drag the grip to set their order.
body.skill_tree: The tree of skills — add children to build specialisations — and whether players may add their own.
body.weapons_table: The columns (one may supply the attack skill), the damage formula and the preset weapons the GM provides. Drag the grip to reorder columns and presets.
body.data_table: The columns — including long text shown in an expandable row — and preset rows, added to every new character or offered as a list. Drag the grip to reorder columns and presets.

body.default: Whether the field can be rolled and how: the dice, the success condition and the levels of success.
body.weapons_table: The attack roll: dice and success condition. The threshold comes from the skill picked in the skill column.

sectionTitle.title: Heading
sectionTitle.body: The heading shown above the section. Leave it empty for a section without one.

sectionColumns.title: Columns
sectionColumns.body: How many columns the fields sit in. A field can span several rows of its column.

sectionActions.title: Order and removal
sectionActions.body: Move the section up or down among its neighbours, or delete it together with its fields.

successLevels.offHint: Rolls show only success or failure.
successLevels.tensHint: One level for every step between the tens digits of the target and of the roll. A failure counts down.
successLevels.tiersHint: The hardest threshold is checked first. Thresholds apply to roll-under fields; a roll-over field shows only success or failure.
successLevels.divisorError: Each fraction must be different, from 1/2 to 1/100.
successLevels.label: Name

modifier.enable: Ask for a modifier before rolling
modifier.disabledHint: Off: clicking a roll rolls straight away, with no modifier.
modifier.traditionalTarget: Traditional rolls — where the modifier goes
modifier.hintRoll: A +20 modifier turns a roll of 48 into 68. The threshold stays where it is.
modifier.hintThreshold: A +20 modifier turns a threshold of 55 into 75; the roll stays raw. With «roll under» that makes the roll easier, with «roll over» harder.
modifier.poolTarget: Dice pools — where the modifier goes
modifier.hintDiceCount: A +2 modifier rolls 2 more dice, a -2 modifier rolls 2 fewer. The pool never drops below one die.
modifier.hintSuccessThreshold: A +2 modifier turns a success threshold of 7 into 9. The number of dice stays the same.
modifier.hintDiceFormula: Each extra die rolls the field's whole formula once more. Edge keeps the best result, setback the worst.
modifier.hintDiceTens: Each extra die rolls only a new tens digit; the units stay. Works on fields whose formula is a single d100 — other fields roll without extra dice.
modifier.diceHint: Best and worst follow each field's success rule: rolling under the threshold, lower is better; rolling over it, higher is. Fields with a raw result and dice pools roll without extra dice.
modifier.limitsHint: Min and max both at 0 means no limits.
modifier.presetsEmpty: No quick picks — the prompt shows just the number field.
